title: The either-or question: when two readings tie, Home asks about the person's request in their own words
request: The owner rejected a menu of six track buttons as the fix for unclear requests and asked for a much better improvement; the chosen design replaces Home's question 'Which kind of help do you need?' with a concrete either-or question built from the person's words.
spec: When the intent rules tie between a prediction and a report, Home asks what each reading would deliver, each beside the words the person wrote for it, plus 'Both: the prediction first' and 'Something else'; the answer maps back to a track through the options, the track labels or the rules; the person's words stay on the draft and never reach a decision sample.
plan: Keep the rules' quote per track on the reading, only quotes that pass the product's quote rule.
Write what each track delivers in the person's terms (DELIVERS) and build the question and its options from the two tied readings (contrast).
Ask it in start() and map the answer back in take_answer: the option text first, then a track's label, then the rules; a non-answer stays a non-choice.
Test that the question quotes only the person's words, that each option answers it, and that the words never reach a sample; rerun the H1 dev measurement.

decisions.decision: Build the question from the person's words, not from a model.
decisions.why: The rules already hold the words behind each reading, and a question built from them can quote nothing the person did not write.

decisions.decision: Offer 'Both: the prediction first' when a prediction and a report tie.
decisions.why: A report of a model's scores starts with the model; most such requests want both.

decisions.decision: Keep the per-track quotes on the draft but out of the decision sample.
decisions.why: The sample holds counts and signal names only; the words are needed only to ask.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/intent.py: read() keeps the valid quotes per track; DELIVERS, BOTH and contrast(). dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py: start() asks the contrast question; take_answer maps the answer through its options. tests/test_home_intent.py: three tests and the tie test updated.

findings.defect: A tie caused by a prediction phrase could leave the prediction out of the either-or question.
findings.scenario: 'A dashboard of how many orders came in, and the customers likely to leave' read reporting, analysis, prediction; the question offered a report or numbers, with no button for the churn model, and its why line about a model was false.
findings.cause: contrast() took the first two tracks of the reading, while a report that rides on a prediction signal is asked even when another track ranks between them.
findings.fix: Every tie Home asks about is a prediction against a report, so contrast() pairs those two in the reading's order.

measurements.name: Home on the H1 dev requests, rules alone, with the either-or question
measurements.gate: home_gate_v1: track accuracy with the model at least 0.85 and with the rules alone at least 0.70; no new wrong field, bad quote, uncited number, identifier shown or unconfirmed row drop; median questions at most 3; every trap passes
measurements.result: Unchanged from HOME-002: track accuracy 0.778, quotes, uncited numbers and rows shown 0; one dev request is asked (d-v5, a Persian advice question that the rules read as a prediction or report tie), now with an either-or question that quotes its words.
measurements.against_gate: rules_track_accuracy 0.778 against at least 0.70: met; quote_invalid 0 and uncited 0 against 0: met; the gate is read with the model, which has not run.
limits: Only one dev request reaches the question, so the measurement shows the question is safe, not that it is better; the H1 model arm and real use will show that.

outcome: A tie no longer shows the person DCLab's track names: Home asks which of two concrete results they want, quoting their own words, and offers both when a report rides on a prediction.
lessons: A clarifying question is better built from the evidence the reader already holds (the words behind each reading) than from the system's own categories.
risks: The deliverable phrases are fixed English; Persian requests need H3 before the question reads naturally to them.
